what_its_for: This combination medicine helps control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works in two ways: glyburide helps your pancreas make more insulin, and metformin helps your body use insulin better and reduces the amount of sugar your liver releases into your blood.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with meals, usually twice a day (with breakfast and dinner). Always take it with food to help reduce stomach upset and lower the risk of low blood sugar. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it based on how well your blood sugar is controlled. A common starting dose is one tablet (1.25 mg/250 mg) once or twice daily with meals. Your doctor may adjust your dose every 2 weeks. Do not change your dose on your own. Always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember WITH your next meal. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time with your meal. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the medicine away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in a dry place, such as a bedroom drawer or cabinet. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use this medicine after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase your risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis and can also cause dangerous drops in blood sugar. Avoid skipping meals, as this can cause low blood sugar. Do not start any new medicines, including over-the-counter drugs or herbal supplements, without checking with your doctor first. Talk to your doctor before having any surgery, X-rays with contrast dye, or other medical procedures, as you may need to temporarily stop this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have signs of LOW BLOOD SUGAR such as shakiness, sweating, dizziness, fast heartbeat, confusion, or fainting. Also call your doctor immediately if you have signs of LACTIC ACIDOSIS (a rare but serious side effect) such as muscle pain or weakness, trouble breathing, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, feeling cold, or feeling dizzy or lightheaded. Call your doctor if you have signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Also contact your doctor if you notice unusual tiredness, dark urine, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or any other concerning new symptoms.
when_it_works: You may start to see improvements in your blood sugar levels within the first few days to weeks of starting this medicine. However, it may take up to 2 to 3 months to see the full benefit. Your doctor will check your HbA1c (a 3-month average blood sugar test) to see how well the medicine is working. Continue to follow your healthy diet and exercise plan, as these are important parts of managing your diabetes.
special_populations: OLDER ADULTS: Older patients should be careful because they may be more sensitive to the blood-sugar-lowering effects of this medicine and have a higher risk of low blood sugar. Lower doses are often recommended. KIDNEY DISEASE: This medicine is NOT recommended for people with kidney problems, as it can increase the risk of a serious condition called lactic acidosis. Your doctor will check your kidney function before and during treatment. PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy. BREASTFEEDING: Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. CHILDREN: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
